requirements.statement: While a schema-version-2 server is enabled, it shall contain exactly auth none or bearer with a non-empty token.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: When bearer is selected, both clients shall use the direct token only for REST Authorization and existing ticket minting.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: If none is selected or bearer authentication fails, clients shall omit credentials only for none and never fall back from bearer.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: Legacy token_path, schema version 1, and malformed auth variants shall fail actionably without file reads or rewrite.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: When -no-auth is requested, the server shall accept any bind and shall not accept -allow-non-loopback-no-auth.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: While a bound no-auth listener is non-loopback or unspecified, startup shall emit a conspicuous network-reachability WARN.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: While bearer mode uses server-owned -token-file, normal restart shall preserve identity and invalid input shall fail startup.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: When an explicit token change is attempted, completion requires all target clients to authenticate; partial failure shall roll back both sides.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

requirements.statement: The system shall mask stored tokens and exclude them from URLs, ordinary logs, status, and user-facing errors.
requirements.rationale: Directly traces the authoritative user requirement.

non_functional_requirements.statement: JSON Schema, C#, and TypeScript shall enforce equivalent mode/token invariants.
Bearer material shall not appear in URLs, ordinary logs, status, or user-facing errors.
Authentication failures shall remain observable and shall never trigger unauthenticated fallback.

adrs.title: Use explicit persisted server authentication for trusted single-user devices
adrs.context: Local device is trusted while the network boundary remains relevant; prior fresh-read and LAN escape-hatch authorities conflict.
adrs.decision: Use schema version 2 nested auth, direct masked bearer values, stable server-owned token-file, explicit coordinated changes, and warning-only non-loopback no-auth based on bound listener address.
consequences: Positive: one explicit client auth owner and stable restart identity.
Negative: manual migration and accepted operator risk for no-auth exposure.
Neutral: existing REST bearer and WS ticket protocol remains.

alternatives.why_not: Conflicts with explicit direct configuration and no rotation.
